export_note: Selected fields from the completed native grade; machine-local paths are omitted. The mathematical grade is preserved.

grade.first_issue: In the necessity direction, the proof does not explicitly exhibit a starting triangle having no angle in \(S\). Such a triangle is required to refute a guarantee from every initial triangle.
grade.summary: The characterization and both main arguments are correct. The sole logical omission is easily repaired: when \(180^\circ/\theta\notin\mathbb Z\), the equilateral triangle is \(S\)-free, since \(60^\circ=n\theta\) would imply \(180^\circ=3n\theta\).
strengths: Correctly proves that a triangle containing a positive multiple of \(\theta\) is winning by repeatedly splitting that angle.
Gives a valid interval argument establishing sufficiency when \(180^\circ=N\theta\).
Correctly establishes the invariant that every cut of an \(S\)-free triangle has an \(S\)-free child.

errors.description: The existence of an \(S\)-free initial triangle in the necessity direction is left unstated, although it has a routine one-line construction.
